text:
First, without doubt, comes this widening
of the breath, almost anguishing,
and the peculiar resonance of the air,
like a great bell in the void,
bringing me the scents
of rockrose from the mountains,
more fragrant for their distance,
and of so many summers together
in my childhood.

Then there is the preliminary
roundabout, with its modest attempt at a garden,
a world abbreviated, renewed, and pure
without too much conviction, and at its far end
the predictable statue and the entrance portico
to the magnificent avenue,
to the famous capital.

And life, taking on
a panoramic character,
the immensity of an instant, almost anguishing too
—like dawn at a campsite
or the entrance to a nativity scene—life spreads out
again beneath the rarefied sky
as we accelerate.

For there is always something more, something spectral,
as though invisibly taken away,
and yet real.
I think of livid districts, streets
or lost roads leading to villages
in the distance, like those in a nativity scene,
and I see again corners of battered brick
and lonely level crossings, and faces
leaning out to watch us, tiny figures
left behind forever, in memory
like road workers.

And perhaps that is all. Around us
facades loom, and people stand on the pavement
at the first traffic light.

translation.title: From Here to Eternity
